synthesis.procedure: Complexes 1–3 were prepared by the same general method. LH2 (0.06 g, 0.26 mmol) was dissolved in methanol (10 mL), LnCl3·nH2O (0.26 mmol) was added, and the mixture was stirred at room temperature for 10 min. Triethylamine was added dropwise, then pivalic acid (0.026 g, 0.26 mmol) was added and stirring was continued for 6 h at room temperature. The reddish precipitate was washed with diethyl ether, dried, redissolved in chloroform/methanol (1:1), and crystallized by slow evaporation over about 10 d to give block-shaped red crystals. For 1, GdCl3·6H2O (0.097 g, 0.26 mmol) and Et3N (0.12 mL, 0.9 mmol) were used.

properties.summary: Dc susceptibility of cubane 1 indicates weak intramolecular antiferromagnetic Gd···Gd coupling. χMT is 32.42 cm3 mol−1 K at room temperature (close to four isolated GdIII ions) and falls to 15.91 cm3 mol−1 K at 2 K. A two-J isotropic fit gives J1 = −0.03 cm−1, J2 = −0.13 cm−1, and g = 2.03. Magnetization at 5 T is 28.34 NμB, near the g = 2.03 saturation value. No SMM behavior is reported for 1.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χMT is 56.51 cm3 mol−1 K, consistent with four DyIII ions. Ac susceptibility of 3 shows frequency- and temperature-dependent two-step out-of-phase signals under zero dc field, characteristic of SMM behavior below ~10 K. Under 1000 Oe (to suppress QTM), Arrhenius analysis gives slow-relaxation Δ/kB = 73(2) K, τ0 = 4.4 × 10−8 s and fast-relaxation Δ/kB = 47.2(9) K, τ0 = 5.0 × 10−7 s. Zero-field FR parameters include Ueff = 37(1) K and τ0 = 2.7 × 10−6 s.
